Not necessarily the retailer. AI moves that same pattern upstream into the reasoning layer. The companies that separate the model from the learning will build a lasting advantage.

[Marin Ivezic](https://ch.linkedin.com/in/marinivezic?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 3mo


Microsoft’s own Services Agreement bars using its AI services or their data to create, train, or improve any other AI service. I find it ironic that Satya finds it ironic. Will Microsoft strike those clauses and grant the distillation rights it demands of others? If not, then this is just a weapon aimed at frontier labs, not a principle. That + the attempt to basically declare the model layer fungible (where OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google differentiate) and relocate durable value to orchestration and the data estate, where Microsoft sits.

[Akshay Kokane](https://www.linkedin.com/in/akshaykokane?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 3mo


Exactly this, and the part people underestimate is how invisible the leak is. Nobody signs away their institutional knowledge in one move. It happens correction by correction, eval by eval, until the model provider knows your workflow better than your new hires do. Consent at the point of use would fix this, but right now the race to ship is winning over the instinct to protect the learning loop. That changes the moment one enterprise gets burned publicly and everyone else starts asking their vendors the same question at once.

[Shawn Bullock](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shawnbullockconsulting?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 3mo


This is an important observation. I'd add one layer upstream. Protecting an organization's learning loop is necessary, but preserving ownership doesn't automatically preserve correspondence with reality. A company can own every prompt, memory, evaluation, and model—and still slowly drift if its internal representation stops matching the environment it serves. For me, the strategic asset isn't just proprietary intelligence. It's the ability to continually reconnect intelligence to changing reality. The organizations that compound the fastest won't simply own more learning. They'll preserve the strongest correspondence between observation, interpretation, decision, and reality as conditions evolve. That's where durable advantage begins.

[Andrew Smythe](https://uk.linkedin.com/in/andrew-smythe-ethical-disruptor?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 3mo


Protection of proprietary IP is now more important than ever, and a robust "orchestration layer" is becoming a baseline requirement. However, while this approach serves as an excellent shield for tech giants and well-funded enterprises, it presents a massive, asymmetric challenge for SMEs. Smaller businesses rarely have the engineering budget or data scale to build out an independent trust boundary from scratch. You have identified a massive market opportunity for whoever builds a SaaS product that democratises this infrastructure for smaller firms at an affordable price point.

I wonder if[Satya Nadella](https://www.linkedin.com/in/satyanadella?trk=public_post_comment-text) ever read the Learning Layer by[Steve Flinn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/steveflinn?trk=public_post_comment-text)[https://www.amazon.com/dp/0230103014/ref=cm_sw_r_as_gl_api_gl_i_QFEGXB5P2Y3JXP6GHPS6?linkCode=ml1&tag=tumroapre-20&linkId=2bd390b7179ba966264a25361b70b45c](https://www.amazon.com/dp/0230103014/ref=cm_sw_r_as_gl_api_gl_i_QFEGXB5P2Y3JXP6GHPS6?linkCode=ml1&tag=tumroapre-20&linkId=2bd390b7179ba966264a25361b70b45c&trk=public_post_comment-text) Nadella is effectively describing Steve Flinn’s Learning Layer, updated for agentic AI and wrapped in an ownership problem. Flinn in 2010 explained how that loop makes the enterprise adaptive. Nadella says companies must own their AI learning loop.
